steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: Technology has wide-ranging impacts beyond just technical considerations. As computing professionals and informed citizens, we need to understand the ethical, legal, environmental, and cultural effects of technology on individuals and society.

steps.title: The Debate
steps.body: Should governments and organisations be able to collect and monitor personal data to improve security? This creates a conflict between individual privacy and collective security.

steps.title: The Issue
steps.body: As technology advances, many jobs are being automated (performed by machines or software instead of people). This raises ethical questions about unemployment, retraining, and economic inequality.

steps.title: The Issue
steps.body: AI systems can reflect and amplify human biases. If training data contains biases, the AI will produce biased results, potentially discriminating against certain groups.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the ethical concerns around AI bias. Give an example. | What is the purpose of the Data Protection Act 2018? State three rights it gives to individuals. | Describe the three main offences under the Computer Misuse Act 1990.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: AI systems can reflect and amplify biases present in their training data. If historical data contains biases (e.g. favouring certain demographics in hiring), the AI will produce biased results. Exampl | The DPA 2018 protects individuals' personal data by setting rules for how organisations collect, store, and process it. Three rights: right to access their personal data, right to have inaccurate data | Section 1: Unauthorised access to a computer system (hacking). Section 2: Unauthorised access with intent to commit a further crime (e.g. hacking to steal money). Section 3: Unauthorised modification

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the three key pieces of legislation: DPA 2018, Computer Misuse Act 1990, CDPA 1988 Be specific about what each law does and the offences/rights it covers Creative Commons is NOT the same as "no copyright" - it is a type of licence For ethical questions, present balanced arguments (e.g. privacy vs security) Environmental: mention e-waste AND energy consumption of data centres Cultural: the digital divide affects education, employment, and social inclusion Always name specific legislation rather than saying "the law says"
